title: admin HTTP server: Authorization header prefix match is case-sensitive and fragile
description: In admin.rs handle_admin_connection(), the Authorization header is parsed with: line.strip_prefix("Authorization: "). HTTP headers are case-insensitive by RFC 7230. A client sending 'authorization: Bearer token' (lowercase) will fail auth even with a valid token, returning 401. This is a standards-compliance correctness bug. Additionally, the bearer token comparison in check_bearer_token uses subtle::ConstantTimeEq but the prefix match that extracts the Authorization header value uses a case-sensitive strip_prefix, so an attacker sending 'authorization:' (no space, or different case) can bypass authentication when no token is configured (bearer_token = None always returns true regardless). More critically: when a token IS configured, the extraction uses strip_prefix("Authorization: ") with the exact space — if the client sends 'Authorization:  Bearer tok' (double space), the extracted value is ' Bearer tok' (extra leading space) and ConstantTimeEq will return false, causing spurious 401s.
